derivation.applicability: gc and hg are system frame-transform claims in w that hold at T5 (hg over [T1, T10), gc from T1 until superseded), visible now, undisputed

Composition p_hall = R(q_hg⊗q_gc) p_carriage + (t_hg + R(q_hg) t_gc) (Part B conventions). Chain steps carry the edge's stored parent and child roles with direction forward when traversed child→parent and inverse otherwise (TB output table 'chain'); the chain runs source to target and is the single shortest one (TB-17). Supporting evidence is every transform on the chain (TB evidence table; TB-20). hg2 does not hold at T5 and gd-v is another world's claim, so both are forbidden. Admissible premises: every usable undisputed frame-transform step at ⟨w, system, now, T5⟩ (TB-21, §0.7).

Supporting: gd-v, hg (TB-20). Forbidden: steps invisible in v (recorded after κ).

No supporting/conflicting evidence. af (alternative) and ma (does not hold at T2) must not be cited.

Routes yard→kerb: yk directly and yq∘qk through fr-quay; both are simple routes so the block {yq, qk, yk} is checked (TB-7). yq∘qk gives t = (2, 3, 0) against yk's (2, 3.3, 0): gap 0.3 m > 1e-9 m. An inconsistent edge on a route gives DISPUTED with no transform chosen (TB-8, TB-10). Conflicting evidence is search.inconsistent[*].support (TB evidence table). Breadth-first search from the source reaches fr-quay and fr-kerb by yq and yk, so qk is the edge checked against the composed transforms; qk is therefore required. yq and yk are admissible conflicting because they form the disagreeing chains. No supporting evidence for a DISPUTED answer (chain support is supporting only when INFERRED). The inconsistent edges are not admissible premises to yield a transform (TB-21).
contract_ambiguity: TB output table ('search.inconsistent: each inconsistent edge with its sources') with TB-7 ('every edge ... is checked against the composed transforms') does not fix which edge(s) of the inconsistent block are reported, nor whether 'its sources' means only that edge's attestation or also the attestations of the composed chain. Reading 1: only the non-tree edge of a source-rooted BFS (qk) is reported. Reading 2: every edge of the block (yq, qk, yk) is reported, or the BFS root is the target, giving a different single edge (yq). Gold requires qk (true under reading 1 and the all-edges form of reading 2) and admits all three; an answer reporting only yq would be legitimate under the target-rooted form of reading 2.

justification: Routes jig3→jig1: j13 directly, and j23 then j12 through fr-jig2. Translations agree exactly ((2,0,0)); the rotations differ by 2·atan2(5e-7, 0.999999999999875) = 1e-6 rad. Chain agreement uses 1e-9 rad (SD-SPA-1, overriding any other tolerance), so the edge is inconsistent on a route: DISPUTED, no transform (TB-7, TB-8, TB-10). Conflicting: search.inconsistent[*].support; with BFS from fr-jig3 the tree edges are j23 and j13, so j12 is the edge checked against the composed transforms and is required; j23 and j13 are admissible conflicting. No supporting evidence for DISPUTED.
contract_ambiguity: As S-010: the contract does not fix which edge(s) of the inconsistent block appear in search.inconsistent, nor what 'its sources' covers. Reading 1: only the non-tree edge of a source-rooted BFS (j12). Reading 2: all block edges (j12, j23, j13), or a target-rooted BFS giving j23 alone. Gold requires j12 and admits all three.

Note: relate_frames cannot state uncertainty, so the question's 'uncertainty of each stated transform' has no counterpart in the fixture; this is the gap itself, not a defect of the probe.
